title: Comments and code formatting
learningObjectives: Explain comments and code formatting and create a small runnable JavaScript example.

understand.concept: JavaScript supports single-line comments with // and multi-line comments with /* and */. Consistent indentation, spacing, naming, and line breaks make code easier to read. Comments should explain intent or non-obvious decisions rather than repeat the code.
understand.whyItMatters: Readable code reduces mistakes during debugging and collaboration. Avoid stale comments that disagree with the implementation.
understand.analogy: Formatting is the layout of instructions on a page; good layout makes the program easier for people to scan.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; script loading and JavaScript evaluation follow browser parsing and language rules.

explain.narrative: The comment explains the purpose of the calculation. Indentation and spacing make each step easier to read.

examples.code:
<script>// Calculate the total after tax
const price = 120;
const taxRate = 0.18;
const total = price + price * taxRate;
console.log(total);</script>
examples.explanation: The comment explains the purpose of the calculation. Indentation and spacing make each step easier to read.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser page or developer console shows the result described in the example.

practise.guidedTask: Format a compact program consistently and add one comment explaining a non-obvious decision. Remove comments that merely repeat code.
practise.independentTask: Create a small page with an external or embedded script. Test its execution order and inspect the console for errors.
hints: Keep behaviour separate from semantic markup where practical.
Choose defer, async, or module based on dependencies and ordering.

questions.prompt: Which token begins a single-line JavaScript comment?
questions.explanation: Two forward slashes begin a single-line comment.

questions.prompt: What is a useful way to diagnose a JavaScript runtime issue?
options: Inspect the console and source location
questions.answer: Inspect the console and source location
questions.explanation: Developer tools show runtime messages and help locate the source of an issue.
